title: Archives
subtitle: zip, tar, and gzip — flip to reveal meaning

cards.meaning: zip/unzip = package and compress in one ZIP; tar = bundle many files (compression optional); gzip = compress/expand a single stream
cards.notes: tar = glue; gzip = squeeze; tar.gz = glue then squeeze; zip = glue + squeeze in one format

cards.meaning: Pack a folder into a ZIP recursively; -p stores relative paths as given
Recursive — include directories
Store relative paths as given (course example uses -rp for a folder)
List, test, and extract files from a ZIP; extract into the current directory
Save many files into a single tape/disk archive, and restore individual files from it
cards.notes: Originally tape archive. Compression is optional (z = gzip)

cards.meaning: Create archive
Extract from archive
List archive contents
Verbose — print names
File — next argument is the archive name, or - for stdin/stdout; must be last among the classic cluster
Filter through gzip (.tar.gz / .tgz)
cards.notes: Add z for gzip. Habit clusters: cvf / xvf / tf / cvzf

cards.meaning: Create a verbose archive named archive.tar from path/
Extract archive with verbose names
List contents of the archive
Create a gzip-compressed .tar.gz archive
- as archive name on create means write the archive to stdout
cards.example: tar cf - dir1 | (cd dir2 && tar xf -)
cards.notes: Copy trees without an intermediate .tar on disk

cards.meaning: - as archive name on extract means read the archive from stdin
cards.example: tar cf - dir1 | (cd dir2 && tar xf -)
cards.notes: Receive the tree from a pipe

cards.front: tar cf - dir1 | (cd dir2 && tar xf -)
cards.meaning: Copy dir1’s contents into dir2 through a tar stream; no .tar left on disk
cards.example: tar cf - dir1 | (cd dir2 && tar xf -)

cards.meaning: Host1 packs . to stdout → your SSH client → host2 unpacks from stdin
cards.example: ssh root@host1 "cd /somedir/tocopy/ && tar -cf - ." | ssh root@host2 "cd /samedir/tocopyto/ && tar -xf -"
cards.notes: Copy from host1 to host2 piped through your machine

cards.meaning: Compress a single stream/file; default gzip file replaces file with file.gz
cards.notes: Use -c or -k to keep the original

cards.meaning: Write compressed data to stdout; leave the original file alone
Append another gzip member; works, but worse compression ratio than one gzip of both files
cards.notes: Prefer cat file1 file2 | gzip > foo.gz

cards.meaning: One gzip of both files — usually better compression than appending two gzip members
Expand/decompress gzip data
Print uncompressed content of a gzip file (peek without leaving a decompressed file)
Write decompressed content to stdout — equivalent to zcat
Search inside gzip data (grep for .gz files)
Keep the original file when compressing (along with -c as ways not to replace the source)
